posts.cooked:
Because I love speculation so much, I figured I'd start a thread for everyone to post ideas about the unreleased details of the new >G products. PTing hasn't started yet, but I gotta get my thoughts and ideas down before I am not allowed to anymore. So, lets get started.

VotM:

Sgt. Steel's name got dropped early. This is possibly the FILTER agent. He seems the most likely candidate to me for using a military title.

We have 1 villain mini expansion. And I think that will be The Host (or a character closely related to it)

We have 7 promos coming, but it doesntly say they are all hero promos. I think there will be at least one villain promo. I think we will see Apostate as one of our promos. An Akash or Dawn promo are high on my list.

We will see hero promos as well. Naturalist, Scholar, Chrono, Sentinels, Parse, and Omnitron-X are the most likely to see promos here.

Edit: I forgot about Environments! Ok...I think we might see the Citidel of the Sun as an Environment. It fits with the theme as a villain centered hideaway. The other one? It might be the place that Prime Warden Fanatic is standing in front of which I speculated as the Hosts HQ. But these possibilities are so open. They literally could be anything and we have few hints to go on.

Broken City:

Exemplar is the former Chairman Pike who has been in hiding since the Organization was taken down by the Dark Watch. 

Pike is up to his old tricks using geneticly modified goons as his lackies. Pike had a hand in another famous villain who was experimented on with his Chemicals. Spite was subject to many test batches of formulas that altered him. And theres more than a few people who think Spite is on the cover of Broken City. I think they are close. I think Pike has perfected some of his older formulas! Exemplar has 5 new lackies, Demon Fist, Grudge, MindPhyre, Karnal, and Cyst. 

Mind Phyre drew the first flag. Thats the exact codename of one of Spite's drugs. 

Demon Fist sounds awfully close to "Demon's Kiss", another one of Spites drugs. Demons Kiss shows a picture of Spite's first engulfed in a red flame. To me, that is very similar to the purple flame around the guys hands on the box cover. 

The other 3 are a bit more of a stretch, but follow me here.

Karnal. Now the word "carnal" means "relating to physical, especially sexual, needs and activities". You could say Spite had a carnal need to kill. It's a little interesting that PL602 compound drug shows a picture of Spite's chest, notably the side where his heart is. Coincidence?

Grudge. PL531 Compound not only increases Spite's damge, but depicts his flexing arm. If a Grudge is a persistant feeling of Ill will, what better way to portray that than with such an intimidating pose? It kinda works.

Cyst. Now, a cyst is a closed sac, having a distinct membrane and division from the rest of nearby tissue. On PL626 Compound XI, I think we clearly see what could be very much considered "cysts", those bulging pockets of red tissue on his monsterous left arm.

Maybe seperatly these are not convincing, but together they form a pretty interesting picture. Pike has perfected and isolated the different chemicals that Spite was injected with and given one to each of his new test subjects. 

 

As for other characters, I think we might see Naturalist and the Sentinels fill out the hero roster as I could see them being good fits around the theme (and I contend the Prime Wardens will be introduced in their own core set)

For Profit:

We have a clear look at our Villains, but the 2 heros to be included have yet to be revealed. I have a strong feeling Chrono-Ranger might fit well here being a bounty hunter. I think the Scholar will round out the 2nd spot. Why? Because For Profit stole a luxuray Yacht, and I think Scholar wants his boat back!

 

 

Ok guys, those are my guesses. Lets hear yours!

I dont disagree with you at all. Thats a great point with Argent and Akash.

I do still think there is a sensible place here for Naturalist though.

The Naturalist now works to protect the environment and the world from those who would destroy or exploit it for their own means. From corporations which bleed the planet dry, to mad scientists who attempt to pull the moon into the earth, The Naturalist has his watchful eye over the world, its resources, and its people, and he has learned a few tricks from his time in the wilderness...
Broken City is now a wasteland and probably full of nasty chemical fallout from Pike Industrial. Naturalist could make a lot sense in this context, protecting both civilian and environmental interests. And even though he has powers, the nature of his shapeshifting lets him fit into a street level theme just as well as a mystical theme.

If he was saved for the Prime Warden expansion it wouldn't surprise me for the reasons you said. But I think he would make sense here as well if thats the direction >G takes.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
I think Steel is a "villain" in that he migh be working with official sanction. We know KNYFE went rogue, AWOL, and probably a few other things. FILTER seems very much psuedo-military and (to our knowledge) they have not react to this, which is unusual. Steel could be their response, sent to bring KYNFE back to stand trial. He could also represent therefore (since he's clearly a bad guy) the more extreme and elitist side of FILTER. Best evidence? Steel is still in his FILTER uniform, badge showing and everything, with some heavy hardware. I think he would not be sporting his badge if he was thrown out of FILTER.

 

This could also help explain why the government and the heroes don't get along in tactics, the heroes came in conflict with a corrupt and zealous government organization and made some politically powerful enemies.

 

Next theory? That is not the original Plague Rat, someone went and made a plague rat to cause trouble. Unless plague rat was cured and spent some time as human he does not have the skill or motivation to create that serum set-up, somebody made it. I suppose it could be the orignal rat, turned human and then willingly becoming a monster again, but equally likely someone subjected an innocent to that transformation.

 

Blue Pompadour is probably a Lobo-esque intergalatic bounty hunter.

 

My gut says the lady in red is not The Operative. I can see it logically, but my gut says it is someone new... or maybe it is simply some hope.

 

Anvil will be incredibly annoying to fight against.

As for who drugged him up? I don’t know. RevoCorp?

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
copied from the villains post:

For the villain mini-expansion, I'm hoping that we get:

The short yellow, beaky person on Rook city Wraith's incap (here).  IF we are following the batman-esque tropes, we are missing a Penguin archetype, so my hope is that the yellow one is a fence who sends out supervillain thieves (such as the "For Profit" crew) to acquire valuable items for him/her.

Such a villain mini-expansion would tie up a loose end (Rook city Wraith's incap) and could introduce some new elements like the For Profit crew (so we can see some of their story before they are put forth as an established, successful team).  We've met the Hippo (losing to Haka), we've seen the Mirror Lady (who seems to have it out for Setback), and we certainly know Heartbreaker encounters Mr. Fixer at some point. It seems plausible that they might star in a mini-expansion, either as Vengeance style villains, or in the deck of a full villain who prefers to remain at arms length.  

 

For the very final villain of the game, I've been wondering if they might do something funky like having the villain (IE, Terminus) be an entire playmat, with different spaces for the heroes depending on if their were 3,4, or 5 of them, and a villain along with- so your team would be fighting a villain inside a massive world-destroying thing to see if the good guys or the bad guys would be able to dictate the fate of the multiverse.  After all- this is a being that (presumably) has the power to alter space, time, and reality itself.  Can you imagine a more tempting prize?  Think of what someone like Citizen Dawn could do with that- she could wipe out all the normals in one go!  Baron Blade would finally have his vengeance!  Infinitor could finally make the voices (ALL the voices) stop forever.

You could have a playmat that altered the rules and had objectives.  Terminus could be a villain in and of itself (that you played on the playmat representing it's world-ending machine), or it could be a place for the villains to try and control, so that they could alter time and space to their benefit...

For the villain promos, I'm hoping:

1. That we learn a bit more about Miss Information.  Her story kind of ends without any real resolution.  She is revealed as a saboteur, and then she's in costume and has managed (at some point) to take out Tachyon. But then?  

My hope is that we'll see her working behind the scenes again, using her knowledge of the heroes to hit them where they are the most vulnerable and put the people and things that they love the most at risk.  

2. Apostate: I agree that there is a lot more of his story yet to be revealed.  so I hope that we see a promo that sheds some light on his lies.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
I just noticed something from the Broken City announcment page.

The ruined wasteland that was Rook City has gotten even worse, now that Exemplar has begun his chaotic reign. His genetic-abhoration goon-squad of Demon Fist, Grudge, MindPhyre, Karnal, and Cyst patrol the wreckage, seeking to draw life from any they find

In Visionary's Tactics cards, we The Seer being grabbed by a mysterious figure. He looks very young in his Vengeance card, so to look so old in Tactics was strange. I think he is being "drained of life". Also note the purple energy in the picture. Similar to the purple energy of the shadowy figure on Broken City's box.

When Tactics first came out I had speculated that this was Spite. I thought it somewhat obvious, with that glove and the shape of the glowing eyes. But, if my speculation about Pike's new goon-squad being perfected experiments from Spite's original drug injections are correct, what we see siphoning life from Seer is one of these new characters.

Which brings me to a far more interesting point. I was one of the first ones who speculated that Matriarch would become a hero during Vengeance playtesting (which turned out to be true!). The crux of that argument hinged on one fact however. Adam has done no artwork in game of a Villain fighting another Villain. So when we saw Progeny with Matriarch in his grasps, I immediatly thought she would be switching sides soon.

If that general principle still holds true in Tactics (and you could make a convincing argument that Dawn's Searing Lance indeed breaks that rule, though I think the disiplinary actions of her own staff don't really count), then maybe we will see The Seer as a character in Broken City fighting with our heros.

The crux of that argument hinged on one fact however. Adam has done no artwork in game of a Villain fighting another Villain. So when we saw Progeny with Matriarch in his grasps, I immediatly thought she would be switching sides soon.

If that general principle still holds true in Tactics (and you could make a convincing argument that Dawn's Searing Lance indeed breaks that rule, though I think the disiplinary actions of her own staff don't really count), then maybe we will see The Seer as a character in Broken City fighting with our heros.
